question.worked_solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. It doesn't matter which equation we pick first, so we choose the easiest one. In this case, the first equation looks like the easiest.

Using the first equation, we can isolate $v$ by adding $u$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
v=u-1
$$

So, we replace $v$ with $u-1$ in the second equation and solve for $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3u+3v & =5 \\ 3u+3(u-1) & =5 \\ 3u+3u-3 & =5 \\ 6u & =8 \\ u & =\frac{8}{6} \\ u & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute $u=\frac{4}{3}$ into $v=u-1,$ then we can find the value of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u-1 \\ v & =\frac{4}{3}-1 \\ v & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=\frac{4}{3},\,v=\frac{1}{3},$ which can be expressed as $(\frac{4}{3},\frac{1}{3}).$
